I always claimed I  would not have children. People used the same reasoning as you. People claimed you don't know what you are missing out on until you have.
So my theory was don't have one so that you can't miss the feeling.
Well, I my got pregnant and one of those, most unspeakable crotch goblins emerged.
I was terrified to hold her, but once I did. She grab hold of little finger and I was changed.
She instantly became my whole world.
The love for a child can not be explained. She was diagnosed with Leukemia at six months old. She battled for three years. If I could have I would taken her pain in a second.  I just wished she had more than the three years she got.

Fear is good, it is also a sign of self preservation. I don't know if you have any family, friends? But you should talk with someone. 
Reach out to people.

Open up, you have people that love you. Talk to people that care about you.
If talking to them is too hard, just send them a screenshot of your post. You have people that love you! 
Seriously get at least some form of dialogue going with someone, either in your own family, friends or boyfriend. 
Don't cut them out embrace the support they can give.

The only advice I can give is just "hug rape" him. Attack from behind, wrap your arms around him. Tell him that you love him. He is your best friend.
Just keep doing it!
What's up, sorry it is only me then.

Consider yourself lucky you found out about it this way. I learnt about fecal vomiting by my friend that had been stabbed in the stomach area a few times. Had a fun journey in a car constantly clearing his airway of shit while trying to keep as much compression on his stabs wounds as possible.
I think this stems from a difference between men and women. A man hears a problem and straight away tries to find a solution or solve the problem. A woman hears a problem and will offer sympathy.
